archetype.name: Gunslinger (play-extending)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who holds the ball to make something happen, outside the pocket or into tight windows, and accepts a heavy load of sacks and interceptions as the cost of his best throws.

report.headline: A broken start, now a dislocated thumb: Tampa's offense waits without him
report.take:
Mayfield has always been a high-variance passer. Across eight seasons he has finished near the bottom of the league in interceptions almost every year, and his pressure-to-sack rate has sat between .36 and .45 since 2021. His good years (2020, 2023, 2024) came when the timing game and the play-extension both landed. He was a top-10 EPA passer in 2024 with a bad-throw rate of 11.1%, seventh-best in the league. This season neither part is working. He sits at -0.274 EPA per dropback, 39th of 42, and Tampa's passing offense ranks last in the league.

The sacks are driving most of it. He has 13 on 118 dropbacks, an 11.9% rate, and he converts 44.8% of his pressures into sacks, the worst figure among charted passers. His time to throw has climbed to 2.99 seconds, well above the 2.70 to 2.85 range of his Tampa years. That points to a quarterback holding the ball in a scheme that isn't freeing anyone, rather than a line that simply collapses: his 26.6% pressure rate is high but not extreme. The accuracy has decayed game by game. His bad-throw rate went from 7.4% to 21.2% to 30.3%, and his CPOE fell from +14 to -14.8. Week 3 against Minnesota, the league's top defense, was the low point: blitzed 26 times and sacked six.

The season line looks a little better than the meaningful football was. In one-score situations he is at -0.471 EPA over 84 plays, with 11 of his 13 sacks. Trailing by 9-plus, he is at +0.288 with 87% completions, which is mostly soft coverage late in games. Week 1's 23-of-28 line was largely dump-offs, with 4.7 intended air yards per throw, and it came alongside three lost fumbles. Third down (-0.475 EPA, six sacks, 8.7 yards to go on average) and the red zone (-0.548) have been dead zones. The 20 completions behind the line produced negative EPA too, so the screen game isn't bailing him out. Two parts are holding up: his scrambles (+0.237 EPA, four first downs on nine) and throws over the middle (+0.251). Chris Godwin Jr. at +0.483 EPA per target suggests the offense works better when it runs through him.

Now he is out with a dislocated thumb, with an estimated return of October 25. Jalon Daniels started Week 4 and starts again Thursday in Dallas. The three-game sample is small, and his career says the floor is better than this. But he was trending the wrong way before the injury, and he returns to the league's worst passing offense. A hand injury is worth monitoring for a passer whose ball placement and ball security were already slipping.

strengths.title: Scrambles still create value
strengths.body: When the pocket breaks down he can still escape. His nine scrambles produced 63 yards and four first downs at +0.237 EPA each, the only consistently positive part of his game. This fits his last two seasons of 378 and 382 rushing yards, so it is a lasting skill rather than a fluke.

strengths.title: Middle of the field works
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers have produced +0.251 EPA. Godwin, his most efficient target at +0.483 EPA per target on 11 looks, does a lot of his damage there. The 19-play sample is thin. Still, it points to a fix: fewer screens and outside throws, more in-breakers to Godwin and Egbuka.

strengths.title: Track record well above this
strengths.body: From 2023 to 2025 he ranked 15th, 10th and 26th in EPA per play. In 2024 he posted the seventh-best bad-throw rate in the league. A three-game stretch against a top-10 defense and the league's best defense hasn't erased that baseline. The base case is that he settles somewhere between this start and his recent norm.

concerns.title: Sacks are swallowing drives
concerns.body: His 44.8% pressure-to-sack rate is last among charted passers, and 11 of his 13 sacks came in one-score games. This is an amplified version of a career trait: he has been above .35 every year since 2021. The longer 2.99-second time to throw suggests he is waiting on routes that aren't opening. Some of it will regress toward his roughly .39 norm, but he won't become a quick-release passer.

concerns.title: Accuracy fell apart week by week
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate climbed from 7.4% to 30.3% across three games and ranks 31st of 32 for the season. Deep passes are 3-of-14 at 13.2 points below expected. The worst game came against Minnesota's 26 blitzes, so opponent quality explains part of it. The direction is still the problem.

concerns.title: Thumb injury and the return
concerns.body: He is out with a dislocated thumb, with an estimated return of October 25, which is an estimate rather than a date. A hand injury for a passer whose ball placement was already sliding and who lost three fumbles in Week 1 is worth tracking in his first game back. Pressure exposure is the other worry: he has been hit or sacked on 19.3% of dropbacks.

trend.note: Passing EPA went -5.4, -13.6, -10.9 while CPOE slid from +14 to -14.8 and bad throws climbed every week. The injury has paused the slide before he could reverse it.

nextGame.headline: Mayfield is out; Daniels gets Dallas's league-worst pass defense
nextGame.body:
This would have been the cure for Mayfield's season. Dallas ranks 32nd in pass defense EPA, 32nd against short passes, 32nd in explosive passes allowed, and 29th in sack rate. It also allows 23.4 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. A light pass rush is exactly what a sack-prone, hold-the-ball passer needs. He won't be on the field, though. He is ruled out with the thumb injury, and Jalon Daniels makes his second start on four days' rest, on the road.

Dallas's defense is also thin. Safety Jalen Thompson (81% of snaps) is on IR, and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (74%) and cornerback Cobie Durant (62%) are out, which leaves the middle of the field and the slot vulnerable to Godwin and Egbuka. The other side is the problem. Dallas's offense ranks 2nd in EPA and 3rd in passing, against a Tampa defense that is 5th overall but only 14th against the pass. For Mayfield's fantasy or prop value this game is a zero; it matters only as a read on how the offense functions without him.

keyMatchups.title: Dallas's pass defense is last
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 0.412 EPA per dropback, the worst in the league, and gets home on just 3.1% of opponent plays. That is the softest possible spot for a Tampa passing game that ranks 32nd. Whether a backup can exploit it on a short week is the open question.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Dallas second level
keyMatchups.body: With Thompson on IR and Overshown and Durant out, Dallas is missing three regulars from the back seven. Short and middle throws, Tampa's most efficient area this season, should be open.

keyMatchups.title: Dallas offense vs Tampa defense
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's defense (5th in EPA, 3rd against the run) has kept games close, but it is middling against the pass. Dallas's offense is 3rd in passing EPA and passes 2.2 points over expectation. If Dallas can throw at will, the game script turns on Tampa early.

nextGame.watch: Whether Tampa's offense under Daniels moves the ball against the league's worst pass defense, which sets the bar Mayfield must clear when he returns.

restOfSeason.body:
Assume he misses at least through mid-to-late October, given the October 25 estimate. When he returns, expect something between this start and his 2025 form. The sack rate should ease from 11.9%, since his pressure-to-sack rate has never been this extreme over a full season, and his rushing (about 22 yards a game) should hold. The touchdown rate of 2.1% on 96 attempts is likely to rise; he threw 26 touchdowns last year and 41 the year before. The interception and fumble risk is who he has always been, so don't project a clean version.

The ceiling depends on whether the offense goes back to a rhythm passing game built around Godwin and Egbuka over the middle. The current mix leans on outside throws and screens behind the line, and both have produced negative EPA. The hand injury adds uncertainty to his first couple of games back.
swingFactors: How the thumb holds up when he returns
Whether the offense goes back to quick, middle-of-field timing throws
Pressure-to-sack rate regressing toward his career norm

bets.reason: Tampa went 0-3 against the spread even with Mayfield, and its offense ranks last in EPA. Now it travels on four days' rest with a backup starting, against an offense ranked 2nd in EPA and 3rd in passing. Tampa's 5th-ranked defense is the reason this is a lean rather than a stronger play.

confidence.note: Three games, a dislocated thumb with an estimated return date, and he won't play the coming game.
